title: personal llm experiment mini-tracker - maya Q1 2026
content:
Purpose: quick personal tracker for LLM inference micro-experiments. informal, quick numbers + TODOs. Not canonical - use for hypotheses and follow-ups.

Columns: id | date | model | variant (quant/ft) | seq_len | batch | route (hosted/dedicated) | avg_p99_ms | tokens_per_call | cost_per_call_usd | quality_notes | status | next_steps

Rows:
1 | 2026-02-10 | gpt-lite-3.2b | int8-gguf | 256 | 1 | hosted-us-west | 120 | 180 | 0.0012 | hallucinations on long context, good perf on Q&A | done | follow-up: try kv-cache retention tweak
2 | 2026-02-12 | redwood-7b-open | fp16 | 512 | 4 | dedicated-eu | 350 | 600 | 0.0026 | coherent but slower at 512, batching helps throughput | in_progress | TODO: measure tail latency under burst
3 | 2026-02-18 | redwood-3b-quant | int8 | 128 | 8 | hosted-us-east | 85 | 90 | 0.0009 | good perf, slight tokenization quirks for emojis | done | add tokenizer normalization baseline
4 | 2026-02-22 | llama2-13b | int4 | 1024 | 1 | private-onprem | 980 | 1200 | 0.0150 | expensive; quant artifacts in long-form generation | blocked | need HW team schedule for repro w/ diff kernels
5 | 2026-02-28 | redwood-7b-open | int8+kv-cache | 512 | 2 | hosted-us-west | 210 | 600 | 0.0018 | reduced cost ~30%, comparable quality for retrieval-augmented prompts | done | add perf SLO check to console dashboard

Quick notes / heuristics observed:
- int8 usually reduces cost by ~40-60% vs fp16 for these models; watch for generation artifacts at >512 seq.
- batching (4-8) improves throughput but increases p99; target per-route SLOs when choosing batch size.
- dedicated routes yield more predictable tail latency; use for latency-sensitive evals.
- KV cache helps for chat/conv workloads; careful eviction policy matters.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run row #4 with latest compiled kernels (PR #987) to see if quant artifacts persist. Connor to help schedule GPU time.
- Add automated eval harness for hallucination rate on Q&A prompt set (small set of 200 prompts). Link -> confluence page above.
- Confirm cost numbers include request overhead (api + networking) - might need to split out platform fees vs raw token cost.

Quick checklist for next experiment run:
- [ ] Reproduce #2 under simulated burst (50 rps) and record tail latencies
- [ ] Run tokenizer normalization for #3 and compare error cases
- [ ] Try int4 fallback policy for llama2-13b on private cluster (if schedule opens)
- [ ] Add eval script to repo and link PR

Notes to self:
- Keep rows minimal; add new experiments as new rows (date first).
- If something looks promising, move to /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/benchmarks with fuller writeup.
- Remember to tag tickets with JIRA-ENG-1423 when experiments relate to rollout changes.

Slack trace references (copy here if needed): #eng-inference thread "kv-cache-tuning" and thread id: 2938475 (search in Slack).

Small log of command snippets I used:
- run local perf (toy): ./bench/run_inference.sh --model redwood-7b-open --quant int8 --batch 2 --seq 512 --route hosted-us-west
- collect metrics -> /tmp/maya-exp-2026-02-28.json (saved)

End mini-sheet. Keep this doc as my personal scratch + quick history.
